_derivation.note: official_fields.json is produced by build_official_fields.py (committed alongside, deterministic, no network / no clock). It curates the STANDARD (predefined) dimensions and metrics of the official GA4 Data API 'API Dimensions & Metrics' schema page. Custom / property-scoped dynamic fields (customEvent:*, customUser:*, customItem:*, dimensionN, metricN, keyEvents:<name>) are deliberately excluded: they are per-property and cannot be cataloged statically without a live connected property.
_derivation.field_id_policy: The fifteen fields the manifest's source_capabilities already exposes keep their platform-side snake_case field_id and carry an explicit source_field = the GA4 apiName (active_users->activeUsers, device_category->deviceCategory, landing_page->landingPage, page->pagePath, screen_page_views->screenPageViews, session_campaign->sessionCampaignName, session_source_medium->sessionSourceMedium, first_user_source_medium->firstUserSourceMedium, purchase_revenue->purchaseRevenue, transaction_id->transactionId). sessions / conversions / date / country / newVsReturning already equal their apiName so no source_field is emitted. Every other field keeps the GA4 apiName verbatim as its field_id, so source_field defaults to it in the generator. This keeps drift_ids EMPTY and the manifest<->catalog gate free of source_field_mismatch (25.4 AC2).
_derivation.conversions_note: GA4 renamed 'Conversions' to 'Key events'; the runReport API still accepts the legacy metric apiName 'conversions', which is what the manifest and connector request. Both 'conversions' and the newer 'keyEvents' apiName are cataloged.
_derivation.count_divergence: Supermetrics publishes 89 metrics / 261 dimensions for its GA4 connector; many of those are Supermetrics-COMPUTED fields (derived ratios, renamed families, per-value permutations of newVsReturning / channel groupings) that are not standard GA4 Data API apiNames. Those land as enrichment_only suspects in the fusion report and are NEVER emitted into the catalog (enrichment is never the authority). This snapshot declares each standard GA4 apiName ONCE.

sources._fetch: curl -sL https://docs.supermetrics.com/docs/google-analytics-4-fields.md -o server/modules/google-analytics/catalog_sources/supermetrics.md   # DO NOT COMMIT this file (enrichment snapshot only)

probe.structural_note: GA4 runReport takes dimensions[] and metrics[] as {name: <apiName>} objects. The probe batches up to 10 fields of one kind per runReport over a 1-day window on the selected property; a field that triggers an invalid_request is re-probed alone so the exact rejected field is captured (never the whole batch).

realtime_incompatible_fields._comment: Story 25.9: minute-grain TIME dimensions are only defined for the GA4 Realtime API (properties/{id}:runRealtimeReport), which pull_catalog_daily does NOT call -- it builds a standard runReport over a date window. These field ids are cataloged (they are valid GA4 apiNames) but selecting them for a catalog_daily pull is a request-build error the section map cannot express (TIME is a single 'core' section carrying both daily and realtime-only dims). pull_catalog_daily refuses them BEFORE any HTTP call with core.pull_errors.InvalidRequestError (invalid_request-class -- the catalog/integration drift signal), and prunes them from the tier-core default selection so a None selection stays valid.
realtime_incompatible_fields.dateHourMinute: Minute-grain (YYYYMMDDHHMM); only defined for the Realtime API, not the standard runReport pull_catalog_daily builds.
realtime_incompatible_fields.minute: Minute-of-hour (00-59); only defined for the Realtime API, not the standard runReport pull_catalog_daily builds.
realtime_incompatible_fields.nthMinute: Minutes since the range start; only defined for the Realtime API, not the standard runReport pull_catalog_daily builds.
